check_text:
protocol.py: 4 biology problems (2 warnings, 2 notes).

1. WARNING MIX-BEFORE-DRAW: Liquid drawn from well A1 in slot 3 before it was mixed: added
at line 36, drawn at line 42
   line 36:  p300.dispense(50, plate["A1"])
   At line 36 liquid was added to well A1 in slot 3, which already held a different liquid.
   At line 42 liquid was drawn out of it again, and the well was never mixed in between. Two
   liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the tip drew is not at
   the concentration you calculated. In a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 3.
   Also reached 1 other well: well A2 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix the well after the addition at line 36: `mix_after=(5, volume)` in a transfer,
   or `pipette.mix(5, volume, well)`. Integra suggests about 5 cycles at about 80% of the
   volume in the well.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Svec et al. 2015: how good is a PCR efficiency estimate
           https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4822216/
   [1d0076666c06]

2. WARNING MIX-BEFORE-DRAW: Liquid drawn from 10 wells before it was mixed: added at line
43, drawn at line 42
   line 43:  p300.dispense(50, dest)
   At line 43 liquid was added to wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 2 more in slot 3,
   which already held a different liquid (this line did it 10 times). At line 42 liquid was
   drawn out of them again, and the well was never mixed in between. Two liquids layered in
   a small well do not mix on their own, so what the tip drew is not at the concentration
   you calculated. In a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 2 more in slot 3.
   Also reached 1 other well: well A12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix the well after the addition at line 43: `mix_after=(5, volume)` in a transfer,
   or `pipette.mix(5, volume, well)`. Integra suggests about 5 cycles at about 80% of the
   volume in the well.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Svec et al. 2015: how good is a PCR efficiency estimate
           https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4822216/
   [47a5f35f44f9]

3. NOTE CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: drug (tube A1 in slot 2)
   line 35:  p300.aspirate(50, tubes["A1"])
   At line 35 the tip went into drug (tube A1 in slot 2) while it still carried pbs (well A1
   in slot 4) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it
   in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong
   there. The protocol does not draw from it again, so this run is not harmed, but what is
   left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 35 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [cead482d7762]

4. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No blank on a dilution series: 12 wells of drug
   line 36:  p300.dispense(50, plate["A1"])
   At line 36 the robot starts a dilution series of drug in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat
   (slot 3): 12 wells at 12 concentrations, each level about 2 times weaker than the one
   before. No well on this plate holds pbs with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve
   has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told
   from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 4 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Add a well of pbs alone, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [5787c454f063]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
